title: Finite reduction preserves the canonical adjoint mates
statement:
Fix the finite-coefficient conventions [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $B=A_{E,m}$ with $1\le m\le n$. All schemes below are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. On their small pro-etale sites use $D^b_{ctf}(-,A)$, the bounded constructible finite-Tor categories, and $Q_T=(-)\otimes_A^LB$. Use pullback, compact supports, tensor, and exceptional adjunctions as in [def-pur-co-smoothness, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], their canonical coefficient comparisons [lem-fix-operation-reduction, lem-coef-finite-exceptional], and the projection map of [def-exchange-projection].

For a smooth separated $f:X\to Y$ of pure relative dimension $d$ and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, put $\omega_{f,A}=Rf_A^!A_Y$ and let $\theta_{f,A,K}:Lf_A^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_{f,A}\to Rf_A^!K$ be the canonical tensor map specified in [def-pur-co-smoothness]. Under the pullback, tensor and exceptional coefficient comparisons,
$$Q_X(\theta_{f,A,K})=\theta_{f,B,Q_YK}.$$
For composable smooth separated maps $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ of pure relative dimensions, the canonical exceptional composition comparison $c_{g,f,A}:R(gf)_A^!\xrightarrow\sim Rf_A^!Rg_A^!$ is also identified by reduction with $c_{g,f,B}$. For a Cartesian square with this $f$, arbitrary $v:Y'\to Y$, and projections $u:X'\to X$, $f':X'\to Y'$, reduction identifies the canonical extraordinary comparison $\beta_{f,v,A,K}:Lu^*Rf_A^!K\to Rf_A'^!Lv^*K$ with $\beta_{f,v,B,Q_YK}$; at $K=A_Y$ these are the coefficient-object comparisons of [def-pur-co-smoothness]. Finally, for any separated finite-type $h:T\to U$, $M\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$, $L\in D^b_{ctf}(U,A)$ and $a:Rh_{!,A}M\to L$, reduction identifies the adjoint transpose $Rh_A^!(a)\circ\eta_{A,M}$ with the transpose of the reduced $a$, under the compact-support and exceptional coefficient comparisons.
